cloudRunEvidence.extraction: Embedded regional pricing table immediately after the Warsaw (europe-central2) record: active CPU 0.0000336 USD/vCPU-second, idle min-instance CPU 0.0000035 USD/vCPU-second, active/idle RAM 0.0000035 USD/GiB-second, requests 0.40 USD/million.

cloudRunCpuBoostEvidence.extraction: Official CPU table specifies a 2-vCPU boost for a service configured from 0 through 1 vCPU. The feature covers startup and 10 seconds after container startup; the scenario assumes 3 seconds startup plus 10 seconds post-start and prices the incremental 1 vCPU at active CPU rate.

cloudStorageEvidence.extraction: Regional Standard table lists Warsaw (europe-central2) and $0.000027397/GiB-hour. Single-region flat-namespace Standard operations: Class A $0.005/1000, Class B $0.0004/1000. General internet egress: $0.12/GiB through 10 TiB, $0.11 through 150 TiB, then $0.08. Always Free applies only to us-west1, us-central1, and us-east1, so no storage/request/egress free amount is modeled for Warsaw.

firestoreEvidence.extraction: Embedded regional Default USD table immediately after Warsaw (europe-central2): Document Reads $0.039, Writes $0.117, Deletes $0.013 per 100,000; Stored Data and PITR data $0.000267123/GiB-hour (approximately $0.195/GiB-month at 730 hours). The first default table values are Iowa and were rejected. Empty query minimum and index-entry rules documented separately.

networkEvidence.extraction: Warsaw (europe-central2) Premium-tier outbound Europe list rates: $0.12/GiB through 1 TiB, $0.11 through 10 TiB, then $0.085. Cloud Run states its 1 GiB/month free internet egress applies within North America only; Warsaw-to-Europe is modeled without it.

fixedAndMarginal.note: Usage component is an attribution at the scenario point; only marginalCostPer1000SessionsUsd below is a finite difference. Fixed daily startup/shutdown assumptions are held constant in that finite difference.

scenarios.scope: MODELED: explicit scenario inputs and official list prices; not invoice or provider measurement

marginalCostPer1000SessionsUsd.method: finite difference: totalCost(profile plus 1,000 monthly sessions) - totalCost(profile); DAU, account mix, MAU, mature history, package quota, registry, secrets and daily starts held fixed; session-derived traffic/completions/history growth scale with sessions; reconnects/day stays fixed.

limitations: Traffic, audience mix, CCU shape, session/event rates, retry rate, package downloads, history maturity and retention are scenario assumptions unless their evidenceRef points to measured observations.

Local HTTP service time is diagnostic only. Cloud Run service time requires a separately supplied cloudRunServiceTimeMsAssumption per measured app request flow; client-side Auth SDK RPC and local JS cold mount are not Cloud Run app request service time.

Cloud Run instance occupancy is a Poisson approximation with supplied active window and concurrency; actual autoscaling, queues, startup, shutdown, min instance routing, CPU and billing need provider-side measurements.
Startup/shutdown and CPU boost amounts and frequencies are explicit inputs, not measured defaults. Local emulator latency and CPU are not substituted for Cloud Run values.

Firestore SDK snapshots, candidate missing point reads, empty-query counts and billed-read estimates are separate. Index entry reads are NOT_MEASURED; query shape, rules and document returns can change billable reads.

Firestore daily operation quota defaults off because other same-project usage is unknown. Cloud Run, Registry and Secret Manager shared free tiers are also not applied; outputs are gross list-price estimates. No FX conversion, VAT, tax, negotiated discounts, billing export, authenticated inventory or provider measurement is included.

Retention storage distinguishes matured starting history from a uniformly acquired 30-day cohort; shorter expiry is rejected, and 90/365-day cases are storage-only sensitivities. Firestore PITR is priced from an explicit assumed GiB quantity, not a refreshed provider configuration; backup storage, Cloud Build, logs, monitoring, SMS, support and other unprovided SKUs are excluded. HistoryRecordBytes is payload only and omits physical Firestore metadata/index overhead.
